Indikator 9 is a supplementary clinical quality indicator within the [[danmark|Danmark]] healthcare system that measures the mortality rate among prevalent patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation during a given reporting period [^src1]. It plays a critical role in the national quality monitoring structure established by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), as detailed in the 'Atrieflimren i Danmark' report [^src1]. 

The primary purpose of Indikator 9 is to facilitate regional and cluster-based comparisons, providing essential statistical data for benchmarking, clinical development, and the political steering of atrial fibrillation treatment quality [^src1]. By tracking mortality alongside other clinical metrics, such as heart failure development, it helps evaluate the epidemiological implications and overall effectiveness of patient monitoring and care at national, regional, and local levels [^src1]. 

For the current reporting cycle, the active assessment period for Indikator 9 spans from July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024, during which mortality among prevalent atrial fibrillation patients is formally measured [^src1].
